draft.title: Fatigue
card: Fatigue is a drop in the body's ability to keep producing force or power. It can cause performance to fall or effort to stop.
fatigue can occur when fuel stores run low, such as phosphocreatine in short, very hard efforts or glycogen in long efforts.
fatigue can occur when metabolic by-products build up in muscles, such as hydrogen ions in hard efforts. These can interfere with muscle contraction.
fatigue can occur when body temperature rises too high, especially in long efforts in hot conditions. The cause depends on the intensity and duration of the activity.
draft.remember: Fatigue can come from low fuel, by-products or heat, depending on the effort.

a.q: Which cause of fatigue fits a very long, steady run?
a.why: In a long effort, glycogen stores can be used up. Phosphocreatine runs low in short, very hard efforts, and hydrogen ions build up mostly at high intensity.
a.clue: Think about which fuel store lasts for long efforts.

b.q: Lena plays a long netball match on a hot day. She slows down even though her muscles still have fuel. Which cause of fatigue is most likely?
opts: Hydrogen ions from a short sprint
b.why: Heat and long duration can cause overheating, which can reduce performance even when fuel remains. Phosphocreatine runs low in short, very hard efforts, not a long match.
b.clue: Look at the weather and how long she played.
